query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Aluminum oxide coating enhances high-temperature oxidation resistance of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr without compromising its mechanical performance.
generation.conditions: Temperature: 1000 °C, Atmosphere: Air, Exposure time: Up to 100 hours
generation.mechanism: Formation of a protective oxide scale that inhibits oxygen diffusion into the alloy
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved oxidation resistance, yield strength retention, and minimal loss of tensile ductility
generation.boundary: Temperature: 1000 °C, Strain rate: 10−4–10−2 s−1, Mechanical loading: Tensile
generation.uncertainty: Effectiveness of the aluminum oxide coating in extreme environments and long-term exposure

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled oxidation test with coated and uncoated samples
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated sample exhibits significant degradation in mechanical properties or increased oxidation rate, the hypothesis is falsified
